thread:
Maria (PM): quick question — thinking about automatic fallback ordering during canaries. do we want regional failover to have higher precedence than model-variant fallback? :thinking:
Ben (Eng): my gut: prefer model-variant fallback first (cheaper & faster) then region. region failover has higher blast radius.
Kai (Runtime): agree with Ben mostly but depends on signal. if GPU OOMs or model-specific KV invalidation, variant fallback won't help. need signal-aware ordering.
Jen (Oncall): from paging POV, regional failover causes huge cascade (DNS, certs). last time we flipped region we saw delayed queues. we should make region a "safety" fallback only when capacity < X or latency > Y for > T.
Rafael (ML): model-variant fallback usually means dropping precision/quantization or switching to smaller architecture. that sometimes changes token distributions and breaks post-processing. want a QA gate.
Maria (PM): proposal: weighted-priority list + signal filters. e.g. fallback_policy: [{type: "variant", weight: 60, signals: ["error_rate","latency"]}, {type: "capacity_region", weight: 30, signals: ["queue_depth","gpu_oom"]}, {type: "regional_failover", weight: 10, signals: ["complete_zone_outage"]}]
Ben (Eng): that JSON/YAML shape looks fine. how do weights map to decision? deterministic order or sampling?
Kai (Runtime): deterministic with a score: score = sum(weight_i * trigger_i) where trigger_i is 0/1 or normalized signal. pick highest score. keeps it deterministic and explainable.
Jen (Oncall): need cooldown windows and a manual "force fallback" button in console. playbook should show which customers were impacted and allow targetted rollbacks.
rollout-bot: alert — canary 2023-04-17-rc2 exceeded p95 latency threshold in us-west: 12% above SLO. Auto-fallback attempted: variant -> succeeded.
Maria (PM): thinking console should display an ordered timeline: detected signal -> attempted fallback X -> result (success|degraded) -> telemetry snapshots pre/post. we also need a dry-run mode.
Rafael (ML): +1 dry-run. also recommend a lightweight eval step when switching variants: sample N requests through the candidate variant and compute embedding drift / log-likelihood change before fully switching.
Ben (Eng): implementation note: need to ensure prefixes/KV caches are compatible across variants. otherwise we lose cache benefits and latency spikes. maybe add a compatibility tag on model artifacts.
Kai (Runtime): good call. let's add `cache_compatible: true|false` to model metadata and treat incompatible variants as higher-cost (increase weight).
Maria (PM): how should quotas interact? e.g., customer-level quota exceeded — do we fallback to cheaper model or throttle?
Jen (Oncall): for quota breaches, prefer throttling + notify first. automatic switch to cheaper model is risky without explicit consent. maybe opt-in per customer.
Ben (Eng): agree. separate axis: cost-mitigation fallbacks (customer opt-in). keep platform-level fallbacks (safety) automatic.
Rafael (ML): corner case: A/B experiment sticky sessions. if we fallback for a user mid-experiment we could bias results. need to annotate experiment id and prefer per-user stickiness: fallback should respect assignment keys where possible.
Maria (PM): so policy fields: `scope` (global | customer | user), `respect_sticky` true/false, `dry_run` bool, `cooldown_s`, `min_sample_for_eval`, `signals` map. samples in console.
Ben (Eng): sample rollout config snippet for API:
```
{
  "policy_name": "auto_fallback_v1",
  "scope": "global",
  "order": ["variant","capacity_region","regional_failover"],
  "weights": {"variant": 60, "capacity_region": 30, "regional_failover": 10},
  "signals": {"p95_latency_ms": 1200, "gpu_oom_rate": 0.05},
  "cooldown_s": 300,
  "respect_sticky": true,
  "dry_run": false
}
```
Kai (Runtime): API shape looks good. need to add `telemetry_hooks` for SLO trace ids and `audit_reason` for each automatic action.
Jen (Oncall): audit logs are non-negotiable. also want the ability to escalate to a canary incident if fallback fails repeatedly (>= 3 attempts in 10m).
Rafael (ML): for model-variant fallback, we should precompute offline QA metrics and store them with the variant metadata so runtime can decide quickly (latency delta, quality score delta).
Maria (PM): who owns the console UX for showing fallback recommendations and a single-click rollback? Ben/Kai or DevEx?
Ben (Eng): Eng+DevEx can partner. Eng builds API + telemetry surface, DevEx builds UX and messaging.
Kai (Runtime): action items: 1) implement weighted scoring prototype in runtime (Ben/Kai), 2) add model metadata `cache_compatible` + offline QA fields (Rafael), 3) console mockups for action/force/dry-run (Maria/DevEx), 4) oncall playbook updates (Jen).
Maria (PM): can we get an RFC by EOD Friday with config schema + sample telemetry signals + failure modes?
Ben (Eng): I'll draft runtime schema. Rafael will add QA metrics.
Rafael (ML): on it. I'll include suggested eval queries and thresholds.
Jen (Oncall): I'll mock the escalation rules and SLO thresholds we actually want.
Maria (PM): thanks all. small UX ask: show "probable behavior" column in console so users know what will happen if a signal triggers (e.g., "switch to quantized-1 (lower perf, -0.7 quality)").
Ben (Eng): good idea. we'll create a deterministic simulator endpoint: `/v1/rollout/simulate` to preview policy outcomes for a given trace/sample.
Maria (PM): perfect. that should help customers opt-in for cost fallbacks and prevent surprises. :thumbsup:
